analysis.title: US Weekly Kickstart: What to own when slowing growth meets narrow breadth
key_insights: Concerns about the rising cost of capital have caused the equity market to downgrade its growth expectations. GS Cyclicals vs. Defensives pair fell 6% over the past two weeks, and rates and credit markets show similar pressure.
GS Prime Services noted a sharp reduction in hedge fund net leverage this week, alongside a positioning pullback in AI-related stocks.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose more than 100 bp over six months but has fallen more than 20 bp in the past two weeks. USD high yield spreads widened more than 20 bp, concentrated in AI-related issuers, while Energy and Utilities credit held up relatively well.

GS baseline: S&P 500 EPS growth of 36% in 2026 slowing to 11% in 2027 on its reported basis. Adjusted for non-recurring accounting distortions to 2026 earnings, 2027 growth is 18%. Forecasts assume modest real GDP deceleration, with a drag from higher oil prices and interest rates.
GS estimates AI capex currently contributes about half of S&P 500 EPS growth. That impulse should fade into 2027 as capex growth slows and depreciation builds.

GS 2027 S&P 500 EPS forecast of $415 is close to bottom-up consensus of $423, implying the run of large upward estimate revisions is likely behind. For 2028 GS is $460, 7% below bottom-up consensus of $492.

Early Q3 earnings read: with 10% of S&P 500 companies reported, 53% beat consensus EPS by more than one standard deviation of analyst estimates. That is above the 25-year average of 50% but below the 64% average of the past four quarters. Revision breadth is still positive but has declined in recent weeks.

Historically, positive but decelerating growth has meant positive but moderating S&P 500 returns, driven by earnings growth rather than P/E expansion. Volatility and correlations rise only slightly in deceleration and jump mainly when growth turns negative. Correlations and index volatility remain near record lows today.

In positive-but-decelerating growth, secular growth beats cyclical growth. Info Tech (+1.1pp) and Health Care (+1.0pp) have historically done best, while Materials (-1.5pp) and Consumer Discretionary (-0.8pp) did worst. Momentum, EPS revisions and low volatility factors have also outperformed.

Breadth is extremely narrow: the S&P 500 is 2% from its record high but the median stock is 15% from its high, near the narrowest since the Dot-Com Bubble. Narrow breadth resolves through a 'catch down' of leaders or a 'catch up' of laggards, and either way Momentum reverses. GS warns to be wary of Momentum exposure, which fell 8% this week.
Russell 2000 and the GS Neoclouds basket (GSXUNEOC) have fallen 10% and 44% since June. Over the past two weeks the S&P 500 ex. AI has rallied 4% as AI stocks sold off.

GS recommends consumer-facing laggards for a catch-up. The GS macro view is falling energy prices and interest rates in 2027 and accelerating real income growth, especially for the bottom income quintile, while hedge fund exposure to Consumer Discretionary is at multi-year lows. The low-income consumer discretionary basket (GSXULOWD) is up 7% since the start of October, and consumer experience stocks are favored for secular growth at undemanding valuations.

For investors worried about a continued catch down, GS screens 23 Russell 1000 Health Care and Consumer Staples stocks with low realized volatility, high free cash flow yield and high FCF conversion, excluding names with 2027 consensus EPS growth below 5%.

Biggest weekly S&P 500 movers: hardware and AI-linked names fell sharply (COHR -26%, LITE -25%, HPE -25%, SMCI -24%, DELL -23%), while FICO (+16%), CTSH (+12%) and EFX (+11%) led gains. Info Tech fell 3.6% on the week, Semiconductors 7.1%, while Health Care rose 5.3% and Consumer Staples 3.8%.
GS S&P 500 targets: 8000 at YE2026 (about 3% above the current 7744) and 8700 at 12 months (12%). GS Equity Sentiment Indicator is at -0.4 (light positioning). The index trades at 19x NTM EPS.

tension_points.bull_case: Positive but decelerating growth historically supports moderate S&P 500 gains driven by earnings, and secular growth, momentum, revisions and low volatility usually outperform.
tension_points.bear_case: Breadth is near its narrowest since the Dot-Com Bubble, so Momentum reverses whether leaders catch down or laggards catch up, and a rising cost of capital is hitting AI names.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growth turning negative would lift volatility and correlations from near-record lows, and a further catch down would favor defensives over the catch-up trade.
